# Canonical Arguments A01–A36

Each argument develops one operation through its claim, grounds, consequences and return. The thirty-six arguments, sixty-four concepts, thirty-six conjugate arguments and their shared A/C root form the complete field. A movement opens only the part its local task needs; the [rooms](../README.md) preserve that order of encounter.

Read an argument through its own sixfold first. Its conjugate follows the same operation into technological practice; its Concepts open the distinctions on which it depends. The pairing below lets you cross between the two faces without losing either. The [A/C root](conjugate/AC.md) holds their common field.

The 21 earlier carriers in `section-rooms/arguments/` are historical provenance. Their successor notices preserve the dispositions; they do not supply a competing live argument sequence.
